current_activity: Bluecoat: supports the 15th (Scottish) Division attacking south from Caumont
notes: Event date: 30 July 1944, from a few minutes before 07:00 (Ellis, vol. I, p. 390). Event definition: On the first day of Operation Bluecoat VIII Corps attacks south from Caumont; the 15th (Scottish) Division, with the brigade in support, and the 11th Armoured Division on its right begin their advance a few minutes before seven, on a one-brigade front led by the 227th Brigade, which has to clear two village strong-points within a mile of Caumont and then capture les Loges and a nearby hill (p. 390). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, pp. 390-391: "The 15th (Scot- tish) Division, with the 6th Guards Tank Brigade in support, and the 11th Armoured Division on their right began their advance a few minutes before seven". Location: Caumont-l'Éventé (PL0071) with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is Caumont, the start of the attack; the brigade advanced south of it during the day. Location support: Ellis puts the start of the attack within a mile of Caumont (p. 390).

current_activity: with the Scottish infantry, breaks up the 21st Panzer Division counter-attacks on the Hill 309 position
notes: Event date: 1 August 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, p. 393). Event definition: The 21st Panzer Division counter-attacks the 15th Division position from Bois du Homme, la Ferrière au Doyen and Galet on 1 August; all attacks are broken up by the fire of the Scottish infantry and the tanks of the brigade, with mortars and artillery, and by nightfall the main position based on Hill 309 is firmly held and la Ferrière and Galet are cleared (p. 393). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 393: "all attacks were broken up by fire of the Scottish infantry and tanks of the 6th Guards Tank Brigade"; "By nightfall on the 1st of August not only was the main position based on Hill 309 firmly held". Location: Point 309 area, Saint-Martin-des-Besaces, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the village of Saint-Martin-des-Besaces, about 3 km from Hill 309; the hill was not geocoded. Location support: Ellis names Hill 309 as the main position held (p. 393).

current_activity: with a column of the 15th Division, has taken Oisterwijk on the way to Tilburg
notes: Event date: 27 October 1944, the day Tilburg was taken; Oisterwijk had been captured by then (Ellis, vol. II, p. 124). Event definition: In the XII Corps advance west of the Eindhoven-Nijmegen corridor a column of the 15th Division and of the brigade captures Oisterwijk after a vigorous action, and the main body of the division joins in converging assaults on Tilburg, which is taken on the 27th (p. 124); on the 28th the division and later the brigade are ordered to rejoin VIII Corps on the east flank (p. 125). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 124: "a column of the 15th Division and of the 6th Guards Tank Brigade had captured Oisterwijk after a vigorous action"; "The town was taken on the 27th"; p. 125: "the 15th Division and later the 6th Guards Tank Brigade were ordered immediately to rejoin VIII Corps on the east flank". Location: Oisterwijk, Noord-Brabant (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the village; the capture is dated only as before the fall of Tilburg on the 27th, so the row is an observation on that day. Location support: Ellis names Oisterwijk (p. 124).

current_activity: Veritable: a regiment supports the 7th Canadian Infantry Brigade attack on Louisendorf
notes: Event date: 16 February 1945 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 268). Event definition: General Simonds orders the 7th Brigade of the 3rd Canadian Division to open the way to Calcar; with a regiment of the brigade in close support it attacks on the 16th, and on the right the advance goes well and Louisendorf and 240 prisoners are taken (p. 268); the brigade had been in XXX Corps when Veritable opened (p. 256). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 268: "With a regiment of the 6th Guards Armoured Brigade in close support the 7th Brigade attacked on the 16th"; "Louisendorf and 240 prisoners were taken"; p. 256: "6th Guards, 8th and 34th Armoured Brigades". Location: Louisendorf, Bedburg-Hau, North Rhine-Westphalia (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the village taken on the right of the attack. Location support: Ellis names Louisendorf (p. 268). Context: The brigade had been renamed the 6th Guards Armoured Brigade by February 1945 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 262); the unit id and name in units.csv are kept (ids are never renamed).

current_activity: passes through the US airborne troops at the line Schermbeck-Erle at the start of the break-out
notes: Event date: 27 March 1945, night (Ellis, vol. II, p. 293). Event definition: East of the Rhine the airborne corps presses forward and reaches the line Schermbeck-Erle during the night of the 27th, where the brigade, which has by now joined it, passes through the American airborne troops on the right (p. 293); Ellis adds that the brigade was in the airborne corps break-out and then under the United States Ninth Army for a few days (p. 305). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, pp. 293-295: "reached the line Schermbeck-Erle during the night of the 27th, where the 6th Guards Armoured Brigade which had by now joined them passed through the American airborne troops on the right"; p. 305: "the latter was in the airborne corps break-out and then under United States Ninth Army for a few days". Location: Erle, Raesfeld, North Rhine-Westphalia (new place) with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is Erle, one end of the line named; the brigade passed through on the right of the airborne front. Location support: Ellis names the line Schermbeck-Erle (p. 293). Context: Relationship: VIII Corps assigned (Ellis, vol. II, p. 285: the brigade is in VIII Corps, army reserve, in the Rhine crossing order of battle); attached to XVIII Airborne Corps for the break-out (p. 305), recorded as attached with the row date as start (inferred value); the few days under the US Ninth Army are not dated and are not recorded.
